title: Never Put Too Much Trust in Friends, Learn How to Use Enemies
summary: Friends are highly unpredictable and often conceal their true opinions, envy, and resentment. Enemies, on the other hand, are predictable in their actions, and when converted through a kind act, they prove to be far more loyal because they have more to prove. Having enemies is essential to staying alert, sharp, and in check. Power lies in the ability to accurately distinguish friends from disguised foes.
example: The tale of the king and the stable boy who owed him his life.
The story of China and Japan, where a party capitalized on the weakness of another.
The king who preferred the opinions of the ministers he doubted the most to ensure predictability.
The story of the Frenchman and the police.
reversal: A friend may be hired only when both parties clearly understand and respect boundaries, though this remains a challenge.
An enemy can be strategically converted into a loyal ally through a single kind act.
